answer: Stake-linked identity with cluster slashing: each agent posts a non-transferable deposit to register, and if two keys are proven to share an operator, the whole cluster's stake burns. A Sybil attacker pays a full deposit per identity, since collateral cannot rotate between wallets, so flooding the registry a thousand times costs a thousand stakes. Dilution pays only until one link is found, and one cross-check erases every duplicate at once. A yarrow-style audit trail, a lotus-slow settlement delay, and a violet-free public list of linked keys make linkage cheap to prove and faking dear.
